data.name: Naasih
data.gender_notes: Naasih is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who gives advice and guidance. Derived from the Arabic verb nasaha, meaning 'to advise, to warn, to help'. In Islamic history, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) used this term to describe the role of a righteous believer, who counsels and guides others towards the path of righteousness. The name Naasih carries the meaning “Advisor, Counselor” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Naasih usually hope their child will grow to embody advisor, counselor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Naasih belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Advisor, Counselor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Naasih total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: ناصح
in_arabic.meaning: ناصح يعني الشخص الذي يقدم النصيحة أو يعطي العطاء بحسن نية
in_arabic.long_meaning: ناصح هو اسم مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ن-ص-ح' والذي يعني تقديم النصيحة الصادقة أو العطاء بحسن نية. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم هذا الاسم للإشارة إلى الشخص الذي يتميز بصدق نيته وحسن إخلاصه في تقديم المساعدة أو النصيحة. كما ورد في القرآن الكريم في سياق النصيحة والتواصي بالخير.

in_urdu.name: ناصح
in_urdu.meaning: ناصح وہ شخص ہے جو اچھی نیت سے نصیحت یا عطا کرتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: ناصح ایک عربی نام ہے جس کی بنیاد 'ن-ص-ح' جذر پر ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے صادقانہ مشورہ دینا یا اچھی نیت سے دینا۔ اردو میں، اس نام کا تعلق ایسے شخص سے ہے جو اپنی نیک نیت اور سچے اخلاص کے ساتھ مدد یا مشورہ دینے میں ممتاز ہو۔ اسلامی تقالید میں اس کا استعمال دینی اور اخلاقی رہنمائی کے سیاق میں بھی ہوتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: नासिह
in_hindi.meaning: नासिह वह व्यक्ति है जो अच्छी नियत से सलाह या दान करता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: नासिह एक अरबी नाम है जिसकी जड़ 'न-ص-ح' है, जिसका अर्थ है सच्ची सलाह देना या अच्छी नियत से देना। हिंदी में, यह नाम ऐसे व्यक्ति को संदर्भित करता है जो अपनी नेक नियत और सच्चे इरादे से मदद या सलाह देने में विशेष होता है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इसका उपयोग धार्मिक और नैतिक मार्गदर्शन के संदर्भ में भी होता है।

in_pashto.name: ناصح
in_pashto.meaning: ناصح هغه څوک دی چی په ښه نیت مشوره یا ډالۍ کوی
in_pashto.long_meaning: ناصح د عربي ژبې يو نوم دی چې د 'ن-ص-ح' په ريښه ولاړ دی، مانا يې دى صادقانه مشوره ورکول يا په ښه نيت ورکول. په پښتو کې، دا نوم هغه چا ته اشاره کوي کوم چې د خپلې ښې نيت او سچو ارادو سره مرسته يا مشوره ورکوي. په افغان او پښتني دود کې، دا نوم ديني او اخلاقي لارښوونې په سياق کې کارول کږي.

in_english.name: Naasih
in_english.meaning: Naasih means one who gives sincere advice or provides with good intention
in_english.long_meaning: Naasih is an Arabic name derived from the root 'n-ṣ-ḥ', meaning to give sincere advice or to provide with good intention. In Islamic tradition, Naasih refers to a person characterized by the sincerity of their intention and goodness of their advice. The name has Quranic roots and historical significance, symbolizing moral guidance and spiritual rectitude. It is used across Muslim cultures to denote someone who is a genuine and trustworthy advisor or benefactor.

data.cultural_impact: In Muslim communities, the title 'Naasih' holds a great deal of respect and admiration, as it denotes an individual who truly embodies the teachings of compassion, kindness, and patience. As a wise counselor, the Naasih plays an essential role in the social fabric of Muslim society, providing guidance and support to those in need. This role is emphasized in the Quran, which encourages believers to help and support each other (2:183). By embodying the qualities of a Naasih, individuals can bring about positive change and strengthen community bonds.
data.spiritual_significance: The title 'Naasih' carries profound spiritual significance in Islamic tradition. As an embodiment of righteousness, the Naasih is viewed as a bridge between the physical and spiritual realms, connecting the guidance of the Quran and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) with the lived experiences of individuals. The Naasih serves as a source of inspiration and hope, reminding others of the importance of staying true to the teachings of their faith and seeking guidance and support from their community. Through their actions and words, they help strengthen spiritual connections within the ummah and contribute to the ongoing dialogue between faith and reason.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah The name Naasih carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Naasih ibn 'Aamir was a prominent poet of the pre-Islamic period (Jahiliyyah) in Arabia. He was also a leader among the tribe of Tamim and was known for his bravery and eloquence. He was killed during the Battle of Mu'tah in 629 AD, while fighting against the Muslim army led by Muadh ibn Jabal.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Hisham's Sirat Ibn Hisham The name Naasih carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Naasih bin Rabah was a Jewish poet from the Banu Hanifah tribe in Kufa, Iraq. During the caliphate of Umar ibn Abdulaziz (717-720 AD), Naasih was a prominent critic of the ruler's policy of leniency towards non-Muslims. He wrote a poem condemning Umar for his religious tolerance and was subsequently exiled from Kufa.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Naasih' in contemporary Islamic context refers to a caring, compassionate, and supportive person in one's life. Muslims on various digital platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, and Discord use this term to express their appreciation for individuals who help them maintain their self-care routines, promote mental health awareness, and provide a safe space for spiritual growth and connections. The use of the term 'Naasih' reflects the importance of community and care in Islamic teachings and the growing trend towards using social media for personal growth and support.
